Subject: Observability egress constraints and SIEM mapping for Private deployment

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec and Platform teams:

1) We need a clear advisory on how Redwood will export logs/metrics/traces from our VPC-deployed cluster to our Splunk-heavy SIEM. AcmeCloud cannot permit any direct outbound to public endpoints without a transit/proxy pattern and signed attestations.

2) Are there established prescriptive patterns for (a) TCP syslog (HEC) over TLS via a customer-managed forwarder, (b) signed evidence bundles for quarterly audits, and (c) low-latency trace hooks that avoid long-lived egress tunnels?

Can you share an architecture sketch and an implementation checklist we can hand to our netops/infra team? Also need to identify what artifacts Redwood will provide for SOC2 evidence.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear asks.

Short answer: yes, we have prescriptive patterns and a runnable checklist. I've sketched an advisory that covers three recommended patterns and the associated evidence artifacts. Attaching a concise diagram and an implementation spreadsheet that your netops team can use.

High-level proposed patterns (summary):
- Forwarder-proxy model: customer-managed forwarder (Splunk Universal Forwarder/Fluentd) in the VPC -> mTLS to customer egress proxy (managed by Acme) -> Splunk HEC. This avoids public egress from Redwood nodes.
- Transit-relay model: a minimal Redwood forwarder inside isolated subnet that pushes to a transit relay (IP allowlist + mutual TLS) hosted in AcmeCloud; good for lower ops surface and centralized routing.
- Evidence-bundle model: periodic signed bundles (SHA256) produced by Redwood Private control plane, stored in customer-controlled object storage (S3-compatible) plus manifest + retrieval audit log.

Artifacts I attached: egress-diagram.png (deployment lanes + proxy hops) and siem-mapping-2028.xlsx (field mappings, sample HEC payloads, auth modes). The audit-evidence-checklist.pdf lists SOC2 artifacts we can provide (signed manifests, delivery receipts, SDK logs).

Next steps I propose:
1) Netops and infra review the diagram/spreadsheet and confirm which pattern they prefer.
2) Redwood provides a 1-2 week runbook for the chosen pattern (network ACLs, port/IPs, cert thumbprint rotation cadence).
3) We schedule a joint-runbook session (30–45m) with your netops to validate firewall and proxy configs.

If that sounds good I'll own the runbook and loop in the implementation engineer.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman

Thanks Aisha — added a couple technical constraints and a checklist for netops below. Sanjay, ping me if you want a separate deep-dive.

Engineering notes (practical constraints):
- Ports & protocols: Splunk HEC over TLS (TCP/443) is our recommended primary. For syslog over TLS we recommend TLS-wrapped TCP (6514) only if your forwarder supports cert pinning.
- Mutual auth: Redwood Private supports mTLS between the forwarder agent and our control-plane connector; for Acme-managed proxies we can provide client certs (short-lived) or a signed token exchange.
- IP allowlisting: We'll provide a deterministic list of egress IPs for the minimal forwarder/relay. However if you prefer no public egress at all, the recommended topology is VPC-private forwarder -> your transit relay (NAT/Proxy) -> Splunk.
- Tracing hooks: We support OTLP exporters; to avoid long-lived tunnels use a push model to the forwarder which tails into OTEL collector running in your infra. Keep batch size small (<=50 spans) and max export interval 200ms for acceptable latency.

Checklist for NetOps (cut-and-paste):
1) Approve topology: Forwarder-proxy OR Transit-relay.
2) Provide proxy IPs and TLS interception policy.
3) Add IP allowlist for: <redwood-forwarder-egress-ip-1>, <redwood-forwarder-egress-ip-2> (we will supply exact CIDRs in runbook).
4) Exchange cert thumbprints and rotation schedule (we recommend 30-day short-lived certs).
5) Whitelist outbound ports: 443 (HEC/OTLP), 6514 (syslog-TLS) if used.
6) Confirm S3 bucket policy for evidence-bundles (customer-managed, block-public-access).

Evidence for audits we can provide: signed delivery receipts (timestamp + SHA256), manifest CSVs for retained logs, and redwood control-plane audit logs for retrieval events. We will redact tokenized values per your retention policy.

Attachments referenced: audit-evidence-checklist.pdf (I pushed a sample to the shared Drive link).

Kimberly Park
Head of Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
